_source: L19 (work plan 2). More of the original's voice, never contradicting it and never a floor count. Built on its own phrases: the Chief's Hall inscription (MEASURE THE GRAIN. COUNT THE FLASKS. KEEP THE DOOR.), the architect and his toys, the bell with no clapper, the scar that misfires every spell, the dungeon still being built. Budget (origins.json): one 'tell' per delve, on its first floor.

tomb: The dead here were laid out in rows, and the rows were counted.
Every niche has a name scratched out of it.
The names were chiselled, then chiselled out - somebody wanted them forgotten twice.
Grave goods, left where they lay. Nobody down here needs a comb.
A tomb cut for one, filled by a hundred.
The lids are heavy, and some have been moved from the inside.
The rows end short, as if the counting stopped mid-row.
Flowers on a slab, dried but not old.
A niche bricked up from the inside.
Dust on everything but the handles.
Two names on one stone, and only one body-shaped hollow.
Someone swept this floor recently. Nobody has lived here in years.
The slabs are lifted and leaned back, every one, from the inside.
Offerings, fresh. Somebody still comes down to pay.
A row of boots at the door, paired and empty.
mine: Someone dug here for something, and stopped all at once.
The seam glitters where the scar has been at it.
The pick-marks run straight a while, then wander like the digger did.
A cart sits full on a track that ends in solid rock.
They were following something down. It was following them.
There is ore-light here, where there should be none.
The air tastes of iron filings and old rain.
A shift bell hangs here, and its rope is worn smooth.
Props cut too short, hammered in anyway.
The lamps they left are still full of oil.
A tally board - names in, names out, and three never crossed off.
Something has been widening this tunnel from the far end.
The props are new timber. Whoever cut them did not go back up.
A cart still loaded, half a turn short of the rail.
The seam runs out, and something kept digging anyway.
Chalk marks counting days along the wall. The counting stops.
fortress: Arrow-slits face inward. Whoever held this was keeping something in.
The gate was barred from the far side.
Murder-holes over the only door - somebody expected guests.
The walls are thick enough to keep a siege out, or a thing in.
A standard still hangs over the hall, too rotted to read.
The well in the yard is capped with iron and chained.
Sand in the braziers, and the sand is warm.
The sally port opens on solid rock now.
Shields stacked for a watch that never mustered.
Somebody chalked the hours of the guard and stopped at the third.
Rust has taken the hinges, and the doors still swing.
The barbican floor is swept clean of bones. Swept.
A watch roster on the wall, every name struck through but one.
The gate was barred from this side. Twice.
Spears stacked ready - dust on the hafts, none on the points.
temple: The altar is clean. Nobody down here cleans.
Prayers are carved low on the walls, where a kneeling hand would reach.
Candles burnt to stubs, and relit since. By whom?
The font holds water that should have dried an age ago.
One god's name on the lintel, scratched over with another's.
Someone still leaves bread on the step.
The bell here has no clapper either.
Offerings in copper, and the copper is bright.
A kneeling stone worn through to the mortar.
The hymn carved here is missing every second line.
They prayed facing away from the altar.
The altar has been scrubbed. Something needed scrubbing off.
Candles burnt to the socket, all of them in one night.
The god's name is plastered over, and the plaster is scratched.
Kneeling marks worn into the stone. Too many, too deep.
lair: The floor is worn smooth by something heavy that came and went.
It smells of old fur and new blood.
Bones cracked for the marrow, and stacked with care.
The nest is still warm. Mind that.
Claw-marks climb the wall and stop flat against the ceiling.
Something counted the exits here before you did.
Something sharpened itself on this doorframe.
Hair caught in the stone at the height of your throat.
The bones are all guild-issue boots. No feet.
Flies, and nothing dead to explain them.
It drags its kills this way, and it will be back.
Bones sorted by size. Something tidy lives here.
The floor is warm and the walls are not.
A nest of cloaks, guild-grey, carefully arranged.
It drags its kills in from somewhere further down.
prison: The cells lock from the outside, and some are still locked.
Tally marks, thousands of them, and then none.
A key-ring on a dead gaoler, and every cell still shut.
Names and dates on the walls, then dates with no names.
The last cell is swept clean, and its door stands open.
Scratches on the inside of the doors. All of them.
The gaoler's chair faces the wall.
A bowl in every cell, and every bowl is clean.
Somebody wrote SORRY at the height of a sitting man.
Chains bolted to the ceiling, not the floor.
The register's last page is torn out and the spine is clean.
One cell has a bed made. Made recently.
Every door is open and every lock is whole.
Tally marks inside the cells, and the tallies run far too long.
The keys are on the hook. Nobody reached for them.
A ration bowl, licked clean, still warm.
works: Benches, tools, a half-made thing nobody finished. Don't touch the architect's toys.
The work stopped mid-stroke, as if called away.
Half a machine, and no telling what the other half was for.
Chalk sums cover the wall - the same sum, wrong every time.
The architect's bench is set for a hand that never came back.
Tools laid out for a job nobody named. Leave the architect's toys be.
A ledger of parts, and no part named twice.
The architect wrote MEASURE on everything he touched.
Gears, oiled this season, in a room sealed last age.
A model of a stair that goes down further than the stair does.
Shavings still curled where they fell.
A door-hinge the size of a man, and no door for it.
The wheel still turns, and nothing is driving it.
Half-finished work on every bench, as if a bell had rung.
The forge is banked, not cold. Somebody keeps it.
Measures and weights, and every weight filed light.
warren: Doorways, chimneys, a street sign - a whole town, swallowed.
Somebody lived here once and kept a window box.
A doorway in the floor, and a doorway in the ceiling right above it.
Washing on a line, gone to dust, still pegged.
A whole street, folded into the dark like a letter.
A doll in a window box. Someone waved from here, once.
A bread oven, cold, and swept out for the next bake.
House numbers running into the dark, and they keep running.
Somebody painted their door blue down here.
A child drew the surface on this wall. Got it wrong.
The gutters still run, and they run uphill.
A chair pulled out, as if somebody rose quick.
The passage narrows until it has to be a mistake, then opens.
Everything here was dug by something smaller than you.
Fresh spoil, pushed out behind you as you pass.
Three ways on, and all three breathe.

descend: %s %s into the scar.
%s %s down past the guild post. The door is kept behind them.
%s %s into the dark below Bellmire, counting the flasks.
%s %s below, where the lamps are lit against nothing good.
%s %s down the guild stair, flasks stowed and counted.
%s %s into the dark - light first, steel after.
%s %s below Bellmire, where the meadow turns to mountain.
%s %s past the memorial and down into the deep.
%s %s on the guild's coin, and the guild wants a return.
%s %s below, boots loud on the first stair and quiet after.
%s %s into the scar with the lamps trimmed low.
%s %s down, and Bellmire holds its breath.
%s %s below with the guild's coin and the guild's warning.
%s %s down the scar while the crier is still reading the name.
%s %s into the deep, and the memorial gets another look on the way past.
%s %s below, lamp trimmed, flasks counted, door kept behind them.
%s %s down where the mountain starts under the meadow.
%s %s into the scar, and the dark makes room.
%s %s down, and the guild post bolts the door after them.
%s %s into the scar, grain measured, flasks counted.
%s %s below while the bell with no clapper says nothing about it.
%s %s down the stair the architect never finished.
%s %s into the dark with the guild's coin already spent.
%s %s below, and the lamplight gets smaller behind them.
%s %s down past the roll, where the names are kept.
%s %s into the scar, and the scar opens politely.
%s %s below with full flasks and a short memory.
%s %s down, boots counted out on the stone.
%s %s into the deep, where every spell is a gamble.
%s %s below Bellmire with the crier still shouting.
%s %s down the guild stair, two abreast and quiet.
%s %s into the dark, and the dark does not object.
%s %s below, past the last lamp the town will light for them.
%s %s down where the architect is still building.
%s %s into the scar with steel borrowed and nerve their own.
%s %s below, and the door is kept behind them, as always.
Down. The air changes first and the sound after.
The steps go wet, then warm. Neither is good.
Another floor. The lamps go ahead and the dark fills in behind.
The scar narrows. Shoulders in.
Down past the last mark anybody left.
The stair spirals the wrong way for comfort.
Something came up these steps and went back down.
The guild's chalk ends here. Everything after is new.
A draught from below, and it smells lived in.
Down. Count the flasks before the dark counts them for you.
The floor above goes quiet the moment the band is off it.
Deeper. The lamps pull in tight without being asked.
cleared: Floor %d cleared.
Floor %d is quiet again.
Floor %d falls silent.
Floor %d holds, for now.
Floor %d is done, and the guild writes it down.
Floor %d - the dark backs off a step.
Floor %d quiets, and something deeper takes notice.
Floor %d won. Count the flasks; one is always short.
Floor %d cleared; the lamps move down a step.
Floor %d is still, and the Chronicle catches up.
Floor %d holds. The scar keeps count too.
Floor %d done - breathe, then down.
Floor %d gives it up. The lamps go lower.
Floor %d cleared - the guild owes nothing yet.
Floor %d empty, and the quiet is the suspicious kind.
Floor %d is behind them. So is the way out.
Floor %d settled. Something below shifts its weight.
Floor %d cleared, and the Chronicle spells the name right.
Floor %d cleared - the lamps get a moment.
Floor %d quiet, and the dust settles wrong.
Floor %d is theirs, for as long as they stand on it.
Floor %d done. Flasks: fewer.
Floor %d holds, and the roll gets a tick, not a dagger.
Floor %d silent. The next one is listening.
Floor %d cleared - the guild will want its cut.
Floor %d is swept. By them, this time.
Floor %d done, and nobody is bleeding badly.
Floor %d yields. The stair down is right there.
Floor %d cleared; the Chronicle writes it in ink.
Floor %d empty, and the air moves from below.
Floor %d holds - measure the grain, count the flasks.
Floor %d finished, and the architect takes a note.
Floor %d quiet enough to hear the lamps.
Floor %d cleared. Something underneath heard it happen.
Floor %d theirs. Bellmire does not know yet.
Floor %d done - the door is still kept.
Floor's quiet. Nothing standing but the band.
Done. Count the living, then count the flasks.
The room gives up and the lamps steady.
Cleared. The dark moves back a pace, and no further.
Nothing left to kill and everything left to carry.
Swept. The guild will want this written down.
Quiet enough to hear the wall drip again.
Held. Somebody sit down before they fall down.
The floor is theirs. For now that counts.
Cleared, and nobody argues with the price.
Last one down, and it took its time about it.
Floor done. Bellmire gets a tale; the scar gets nothing.

lord_intros.hollow_king: The braziers in the hall burn blue, and then burn cold.
lord_intros.grubmother: The floor is wet, and getting wetter.
lord_intros.rattling_host: Somewhere ahead, something counts its own bones out loud.
lord_intros.nightwing: Every torch on the floor gutters at once.
lord_intros.gravewyrm: The dungeon was built around this, and it knows it.
lord_intros.ossuary_lord: It has waited a very long time. A little longer is nothing.
lord_intros.pale_duchess: A lady laughs somewhere ahead, very politely.
lord_intros.mourncoil: Breath steams. Then the steam freezes.

unique_intros.mother_silk: The threads across the doorway are new.
unique_intros.weeping_bowman: A string twangs in the dark, and something weeps after it.
unique_intros.cinderjack: Someone has been playing with the firepits.
unique_intros.kept: A voice the guild knew calls a name the guild remembers.

lord_intros_alt._note: C-cycle 8. Extra intro lines for the SAME eight lords - no new lords. Pick at random from [lord_intros[key]] + lord_intros_alt[key] so a second sighting on one stream does not read identically.
hollow_king: Blue light under the door, and no heat in it.
Something cold is already seated in the hall.
The braziers lean towards whatever just walked in.
The hall is colder at the far end than at the door.
A crown's worth of blue light, and nothing wearing it yet.
The fires burn and give nothing back.
grubmother: The wet reaches the boots before the sound does.
The walls move, and it is not the walls.
Something is birthing in the dark ahead, and not stopping.
The floor gives under the boot and does not spring back.
Something ahead is full and still feeding.
The wet is warm. That is the worst of it.
rattling_host: A hundred small knocks, all keeping time.
The dark ahead has too many elbows.
It counts up, and it never reaches an end.
A great many small bones, all in a hurry.
Something ahead is taking stock of itself.
The count carries down the corridor, and it is rising.
nightwing: A draught from the ceiling, and the ceiling has wings.
The torches lie flat and stay flat.
Something crosses the lamp twice before you look up.
The lamps duck all together, as if something passed over.
The ceiling is closer than it was, and breathing.
Two shadows for every one thing above you.
gravewyrm: The corridor ahead is a throat.
The stone trembles in long, patient breaths.
Older than the guild, older than the scar - and still hungry.
The walls were cut to let this thing pass, a long age ago.
The floor lifts, very slightly, and settles.
This was never a dungeon. It was a den.
ossuary_lord: The bones on the floor are getting up in order.
It does not hurry. It has never had to.
Somewhere ahead, a hand is arranging the dead.
The dead ahead are sorting themselves into ranks.
A dry sound of stacking, somewhere past the lamp.
pale_duchess: She is already holding the room. You are late.
Someone apologises, sweetly, for what comes next.
The air ahead is warmer, and scented, and wrong.
Somebody is being gracious at you out of the dark.
She has had the room swept for your arrival.
mourncoil: Breath hangs in the air and does not move on.
Frost climbs the walls towards you.
The lamp's own heat gives up first.
Ice on the steel before the first blow.
The cold comes in coils, and tightens.

unique_intros_alt._note: C-cycle 8. Extra intro lines for the SAME five rare uniques. Same pick rule as lord_intros_alt.
gnawbone: Something is eating the wall, and gaining.
Teeth on stone, all the way down the corridor.
The squeal comes from inside the masonry.
Mortar dust on the floor, and more of it every heartbeat.
There is a hole in that wall that was not there, and it is widening.
mother_silk: The doorway has been re-strung since this morning.
Everything in this room is wrapped and waiting.
Threads tug at the lamp before you touch them.
The lamp catches a thousand threads, all of them new.
Something tidied this room and left the bundles upright.
The silk goes taut, somewhere behind you.
weeping_bowman: A bowstring, then a sob, then nothing.
An arrow in the doorframe, still humming.
He is sorry already, and he will shoot anyway.
A notch, a breath, a sob. In that order.
He aims through tears and does not miss for them.
Grief, and a very good bow.
cinderjack: Every firepit on the floor is lit, and lit wrong.
Footprints burnt into the stone, going both ways.
Something laughs, and the flames laugh along.
Ash footprints, and the ash is warm.
Every lamp on the floor burns green for a moment.
Something is laughing in the firepit, and the firepit agrees.
kept: The guild wrote this name down as lost. It is not lost.
A familiar voice, saying a familiar name, wrongly.
Somebody the roll calls dead calls the roll.
The roll says this one is dead. The roll is wrong, or the voice is.
It wears a guild cloak and remembers the words.
Somebody the guild buried is calling the muster.

lord: Hold the line, not the ground.
It carries a note. Make it short.
'That is the one the Chronicle names.'
'Let it be noted that I came anyway.'
trap: Stand clear - I will tread it.
'That was a floor a moment ago.'
'The guild should chalk these. The guild should pay me to chalk these.'
hurt: Hold the door, I will keep.
'That one is going in the Chronicle.'
drink: That is the last of it.
'The apothecary counted this one out loud.'
misfire: That wasn't the spell I cast.
Not my spell. Not my fault.
That is not what I said.
The scar is in a mood.
I will try again. Stand back.
%s's %s goes wrong - the scar answers (%d vs DC %d).
%s reaches for %s and the scar hands back something else (%d vs DC %d).
%s's %s comes out sideways - wild magic (%d vs DC %d).
%s's %s turns in their hand - the scar answers (%d vs DC %d).
%s tries %s and the ground gives it back wrong (%d vs DC %d).
%s's %s unravels mid-word - wild magic (%d vs DC %d).
%s casts %s; the scar casts something else (%d vs DC %d).
%s shapes %s and the scar bends it (%d vs DC %d).
%s's %s answers to the ground instead (%d vs DC %d).
%s speaks %s; something else finishes it (%d vs DC %d).
%s's %s slips the words - wild magic (%d vs DC %d).
%s calls %s and the scar calls louder (%d vs DC %d).
%s's %s breaks apart over the stone (%d vs DC %d).
%s offers %s to the scar, and the scar keeps it (%d vs DC %d).
epitaphs: Measured the grain. Counted the flasks. Kept the door.
The scar keeps what it takes.
Went down with a lamp. Did not come up.
The guild writes the name and keeps it.
Somewhere below, a bell with no clapper rings once.
One floor too many.
Lit a lamp. The dark kept it.
Counted every flask but the last.
The guild writes the name; the scar keeps the rest.
Measured the grain. The grain ran out.
Went down proving something. Proved it.
Kept the door, until the door kept them.
The bell with no clapper rang, and they did not come up.
Named on the roll, and marked with a dagger.
Paid the guild's price in full.
The door held. They did not.
Last seen going down, lamp high.
The Chronicle spells the name right, at least.
Fed the scar and asked for nothing.
A good hand with a flask, to the end.
Kept the door one floor too long.
Took the stair down and the guild's coin with it.
Knew the shapes. Met a new one.
Walked in light, left in the dark.
The lamp came back. They did not.
Marked present on the roll, and absent everywhere else.
Trimmed the lamp low to save oil. Saved oil.
Bellmire remembers the name and nothing else.
Went down for the gold and found the rest of it.
Mended everyone but themselves.
The flask was full. The hand was slow.
Stood where the floor lied.
No body to bury. The guild buried the name.
Measured the grain. Did not measure the dark.
Kept the door. Lost the room.
The lamp was lit. That is something.
Brought everyone else up.
Went down for a friend. Stayed with them.
Never once short on flasks.
The guild's ledger is square. The rest is not.
Came up as a name on a list.
Knew better and went anyway.
Stood where the lord swung.
Spent the last flask on somebody else.
The dark took the lamp, the coat and the rest.
Counted the flasks for the whole band.
Bought the stair with their own back.
Answered the crier. Did not answer the roll.
Died rich, two floors from the surface.
Held the stair while the others climbed.
No last words. Plenty of warning.
The scar misfired, and so did the luck.
Mended the door, if not the hand.
Last of the lamp oil, first into the room.
Marked with a dagger on the Guild Roll.
The flask was empty and the hand was steady.
Took the deep road for the guild's coin.
The bell with no clapper kept its silence.
Kept the door until the door went.
Measured twice. The dark measured once.
Carried the lamp for everyone else.
Paid the ferryman early.
Went in first. Always went in first.
The band came up. Not all of it.
Named on the roll, and the roll is kept.
Stood where standing was the whole job.
Last flask given away, and gladly.
Brave, loud, and brief.
The scar took a good one.
Walked down smiling. Bellmire remembers that much.
Spent every copper on the right things.
Nothing left behind but the chalk marks.
Fell on a floor nobody has a name for.
Counted the flasks. There were none left to count.

forge.1: Bellmire iron: honest, dull, and better than bare hands.
forge.2: Folded twice; the smith signs it.
forge.3: Runes along the fuller smoulder when it is drawn.
forge.4: Dragontooth - nobody in Bellmire will say whose tooth.
forge.5: Scarforged. It hums when the dark is near.

forge_alt._note: C-cycle 12. Extra forge-tier descriptions for the SAME five tiers - no new tiers. Pick at random from [forge[tier]] + forge_alt[tier] so a tier's line does not read identically every time a weapon is named. Keys are the same tier strings as forge.
1: Plain Bellmire work. It will not sing, and it will not snap.
Dull as a ditch, honest as a measure. It holds an edge long enough.
Town iron. The smith is not proud of it and will not take it back.
2: Folded twice and stamped. The smith puts her mark where you can see it.
Twice-worked steel. It rings true when you knock it.
Good enough that the smith wrote her name on it.
3: Runes down the fuller wake when it is drawn, and sulk when it is sheathed.
The marks along the blade hold a low heat. Nobody will say who cut them.
Drawn, it glows faint along the groove. Sheathed, it waits.
4: Dragontooth. Bellmire will sell it to you and still not say whose tooth.
Tooth-forged. It bites first and asks after.
Cut from something that had teeth to spare. One tooth, one blade.
5: Scarforged. It hums when the dark leans close, and it has never been wrong yet.
Quenched in the scar. It knows what is coming before you do.
Forged where the ground misfires. It keeps the habit.

town_levels_for_the_desktop._note: For the desktop's town.gd if it wants them (the laptop does not edit town.gd): an announcement when Bellmire reaches a level, in the original's voice.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.1: Bellmire is a hamlet with a hole in it.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.2: Bellmire is a village now. The guild post has a door.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.3: Bellmire stands as a market town. Measure the grain.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.4: Bellmire grows into a town of note. Count the flasks.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.5: Bellmire is a walled town. Keep the door.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.6: Bellmire is a city in all but charter.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.7: Bellmire is a city. The scar is still deeper than it was.

e3po._note: E3PO - Commander of the Guards. He CANNOT die; badly hurt he withdraws to the barracks, heals, and returns. Immortal, beloved, a little pompous, utterly reliable. For the desktop's raids.gd/town.gd if it wires him (content worker never touches code). Additive; dead until wired.
intro: E3PO takes the wall. The whole guard stands straighter.
The Commander is on the field. Nobody tells him to be careful.
The gate opens, and it is only E3PO coming out to meet them.
E3PO arrives at a walk. Running would suggest doubt.
The Commander's voice reaches the back of the square before he does.
E3PO comes up the stair to the wall at the same pace he always does.
The Commander takes his place at the gate and the guard stop checking the horizon.
E3PO arrives already giving orders, which saves everyone a moment.
withdraw: E3PO is hauled to the barracks, swearing he is fine.
The Commander falls back to heal. He will be back before you miss him.
Too much even for E3PO - he withdraws to the barracks.
They carry E3PO off the wall. 'A scratch,' he says, bleeding freely.
E3PO goes down on one knee and the whole wall goes quiet. Then he swears, and it starts breathing again.
The Commander is carried off still giving orders over a shoulder.
'Barracks. Briefly.' E3PO lets himself be helped, which costs him more than the wound.
The Commander is walked off the wall between two guards and complains about both.
E3PO withdraws, insisting the barracks was his idea.
They take E3PO's helm off and he asks for it straight back.
return: E3PO is back on the wall, mended and mortified.
The Commander returns to duty. He apologises to no one.
E3PO retakes the gate, good as new and twice as loud.
E3PO walks out of the barracks buckling the last strap. 'Where were we.'
The Commander returns with fresh bandages and the same volume.
E3PO is back, and the raiders can tell from the far field.
The Commander is on the wall again, and the wall notices.
E3PO comes back up the stair at the same pace he went down it, which is the point.
The barracks door bangs open. The Commander has decided he is finished healing.
says: Hold the line. The line holds because I say so.
I have died exactly never. Let us keep the record.
Measure the grain, count the flasks, and leave the gate to me.
A guard who runs is a guard I must replace, and I hate paperwork.
They do not pay me to fall. They do not pay me at all - I simply refuse to leave.
The door stays shut. That is the whole job, and I am very good at it.
Wounded? I prefer 'briefly inconvenienced'.
Bellmire sleeps because I do not.
Shapes, not numbers. That goes for raiders too.
I do not require a monument. A kept door will do.
If the gate holds and the grain is counted, the day is a success. The rest is weather.
Call me Commander. 'Sir' is for men who might retire.
Shut the door, count the grain, and let me worry about the rest.
Courage is a habit. Start with standing still.
I was here before the wall. I will be here after it, if the masons keep this up.
A quiet night is the best work we ever do, and nobody writes it down.
The scar can have the deep. It cannot have the doorstep.
I do not need you brave. I need you where I put you.
Twenty years and no one has got past me. I would call that a record; I call it Tuesday.
If you must run, run toward something. Preferably me.
town_talk: They say E3PO has held the gate since before there was a gate.
Old-timers swear E3PO has outlived three of his own gravestones.
The children drill with sticks and name the loudest one E3PO.
No raider has taken the Keep door while the Commander draws breath - which is to say, never.
The guild keeps a chair for E3PO at every feast. He never sits; he watches the door.
The Watch say the Commander's armour has more dents than the gate has nails.
There is a standing wager at the tavern on what could fell E3PO. Nobody has collected.
The masons built the new wall a hand taller because he asked twice.
They tried to carve him a statue. He made them turn it to face the door.
Every recruit hears the same first words: 'The door stays shut.'
The Watch say the Commander sleeps standing up, and only to set an example.
They reckon E3PO has worn out more armourers than armour.
A child asked the Commander what he is afraid of. He thought about it for a long time and said 'paperwork'.
The bakers keep him a loaf he never takes, and bake it anyway.
Two generations of this town have been told off by the same man in the same voice.
Nobody can name the day E3PO arrived, which is how you know the story is old.
e3po._note_extras: Added keys (C-cycle 5): raid / disaster / festival lines, and viewer_roll keyed by outcome (crit, high, low, fumble) for the d20. Same voice as 'says'. Additive; dead until wired.
raid: E3PO plants himself in the gateway. 'This far. No further, and I am being generous.'
The Commander walks the wall at a stroll, which is somehow worse for the raiders.
'Form up on me! I am the easiest thing on this field to find.'
E3PO takes a blow meant for a bowman, then tells the bowman off for standing there.
'They brought ladders. Charming. Fetch the poles.'
The Commander counts the raiders aloud. The guard find it steadying. The raiders do not.
'Nobody dies tonight on my watch. I have written it down, so it is official.'
E3PO shoulders the gate shut with a raider still arguing on the other side.
The Commander puts himself in the worst gap on the wall and stays there.
'They want the door. They may have a conversation with me instead.'
E3PO catches a ladder on his shoulder and walks it back off the wall.
'Steady. I have done this more times than you have had opinions.'
disaster: E3PO has the bucket line running before anyone thinks to ask him.
'Fire does not negotiate. Neither do I. Pass the buckets.'
The Commander carries two children out of the smoke and apologises for the noise.
'A disaster is a raid with worse manners. Work the problem.'
E3PO stands in the floodwater directing carts, soaked to the breastplate.
'Grain to the Keep, flasks to the chapel, people first. Move.'
The Commander does not sleep while the town is burning, drowning or shaking.
'Count the living twice. Then count them again for me.'
'Nobody panics on my watch. There is a queue for that and it is closed.'
The Commander hauls on the rope with the rest and out-pulls two of them.
'Save the people, then the stores, then the building. In that order. Always.'
E3PO walks the wreckage all night lifting beams off whoever is under them.
festival: E3PO attends the feast in full harness and declines a chair, as always.
'Dance. Someone has to watch the door while you do.'
The Commander judges the pie contest and refuses to be bribed, loudly, for an hour.
E3PO is talked into one dance and performs it like a drill.
'Festival rules: drink what you like. The gate stays shut.'
They hand the Commander a flower crown. He wears it over the helm.
E3PO lifts a cup to the dead, names every one, and goes back to the wall.
The Commander inspects the bonfire for safety, twice, and is overruled by everyone.
'Enjoy yourselves. I shall be over there, being responsible, loudly.'
E3PO toasts the Watch by name, every one, and keeps them standing for it.

crit: 'Now THAT is how it is done. Write it down. Write it twice.'
The Commander salutes. From E3PO, that is a parade.
'Were you trained by me? No? Then you are frighteningly talented.'
'Outstanding. I shall be insufferable about this for a week.'
The Commander takes off his helm for that one. He does not do that.
high: The Commander nods once. The guild post treats it as a medal.
'Solid work. Do it again and I may learn your name.'
E3PO grunts. From him, that is applause.
low: 'Luck is a resource and you have spent yours. Use skill.'
The Commander looks away politely, which is worse than shouting.
'We will say the dice were tired.'
'The dice are not your friend. I am barely your friend. Try skill.'
'That will do. It will not do twice.'
fumble: 'I have seen worse. I have not seen worse today.'
The Commander writes something in his book. It is not your name spelled kindly.
'Stand up. Dust off. The dice do not get the last word. I do.'
'Everyone gets one. That was yours. Spend the next better.'
The Commander sighs the sigh of a man who has seen three hundred years of this.

town_life._note: Ambient Bellmire flavour as the town grows - crier calls, market and guild chatter, building news. For the desktop's town.gd if it wires a ticker; content worker never touches code. Additive; dead until wired.
crier: Grain measured, flasks counted, door kept - Bellmire stands another day!
Fresh off the river: trout, and a tale with every one.
The guild takes names at the post. Bring your own courage.
Lamps lit, walls walked, all's well - or well enough.
Another delver down the scar. Put a copper on them coming back up.
Walls walked, gates kept, and the bell has nothing to say!
Caravan on the road - bring coin or bring your back!
New names on the guild post. Read them while they are fresh.
The apothecary has flasks and the guild has holes to put them in!
Taxes measured, not guessed - the Hall says so.
Rain by evening. The crier is never wrong twice running.
Measure the grain, count the flasks, keep the door - and the crier keeps his voice!
Two up from the scar this morning, and both of them walking!
The bell has no clapper and even less to say. All's well!
Market day! Bring coin, bring elbows!
The Watch walked the wall twice and found nothing worth a second turn.
Flasks on the shelf, grain in the measure - Bellmire keeps its own accounts!
A lord came up out of the scar and went back down in pieces - hear it twice for a copper!
E3PO stood the night gate himself. Sleep easy, Bellmire.
market: Two coppers the carp, and the carp is grinning.
Dye by the ounce - name a colour, Bellmire keeps it now.
Scarglass! Cheap, and only slightly cursed!
Boots that have walked further than you have, half off.
Ale by the jug, and the jug is honest.
Nails, hooks, and a hammer that has seen things!
Salt off the coast road - you will taste the journey.
Wool off the hill, and it still smells of the hill.
Bread this morning; bread-shaped by this afternoon.
Lamp oil! Burns slow, and you will want the slow sort.
Rope by the fathom, and it has held a man before!
Scarstone, polished - it only looks at you a little!
Candles! Burn one for the delvers, buy two for yourself!
Hooks, lines, and a river that owes you nothing!
Cheese with a crust you could roof a barn with!
Fresh ink and honest parchment - write home while you still can!
A hat that has never once been rained on. Not once!
Secondhand steel - all of it came back up. Most of it alone.
growth: The masons raised a new course on the wall today.
A second well dug, and the queue at the first one shorter.
They are building where the fields used to stop.
The guild post has two doors now. Both kept.
The smith has an apprentice, and the apprentice has eyebrows. For now.
A proper gate, hung and swinging true.
The road out is cobbled as far as the ford.
They are putting glass in the chapel windows.
A second row of stalls, and a queue for them.
The barracks took on ten more. E3PO looked almost pleased.
The ditch is dug, the stakes are in, and the masons are measuring stone.
A new row of chimneys on the east side, all of them smoking.
They have hung a lamp at the ford. It burns all night now.
The guild post took on a clerk, and the clerk took on a queue.
A tannery, downwind - and the town voted on which wind.
The market square has flagstones where the mud was.
A second smith, and the two of them already disagree.
They are cutting a road where the fields used to stop.

propositions._note: Viewer-voting town laws (T4). 17 across law/taxes/militia/building/faith/outsiders. Each names a CONSEQUENCE, good and bad - a law that only helps is boring. Readable at a glance. Dead until wired.

entries.title: The Gallows Law
entries.flavour: Thieves hang, not fine. The guild says it will clear the market of cutpurses.
entries.good: Crime falls; the market feels safe to spend in.
entries.bad: The desperate turn to worse than theft, and some good hands leave town.

entries.title: Trial by the Roll
entries.flavour: Let the accused delve the scar. Come back up, and you walk free.
entries.good: Wildly popular on stream, and the dungeon runs hot.
entries.bad: The innocent die below, and the guild loses good names.

entries.title: Debtors' Pardon
entries.flavour: Wipe the slate. Come spring, no one in Bellmire owes a copper.
entries.good: The poor breathe again; loyalty climbs.
entries.bad: The lenders shut their purses, and coin stops moving.

entries.title: Raise the Grain Tithe
entries.flavour: A heavier cut of every harvest goes to the town coffers.
entries.good: The treasury swells; walls and wages get paid.
entries.bad: Full barns, thin bellies - the folk grumble, and some go hungry.

entries.title: The Free Market Charter
entries.flavour: Drop the market tolls. Any trader sells in Bellmire toll-free.
entries.good: Caravans flock in; the stalls overflow.
entries.bad: The coffers thin, and the guild's grip slips.

entries.title: Toll at the Ford
entries.flavour: A copper to cross, paid to the Ferryman, paid to the town.
entries.bad: Traders grumble, some ford downstream, and the Ferryman is not thanked.

entries.title: Raise the Militia Levy
entries.flavour: Every household sends a hand to the wall.
entries.good: The guard doubles; raiders think twice.
entries.bad: Fewer hands in the fields - the town is safer but poorer.

entries.title: Arm the Delvers
entries.flavour: Guild steel for anyone who will hold the gate.
entries.bad: Armed and idle men make their own trouble.

entries.title: Night Curfew
entries.flavour: Lamps out, doors barred, the Watch walks till dawn.
entries.good: No raid slips in by night.
entries.bad: The taverns empty; the folk feel watched, not kept.

entries.title: Wall the Town
entries.flavour: Stone where the fields stop. The masons are ready and waiting.
entries.bad: It costs a fortune, and the harvest waits while the masons build.

entries.title: Dig the Second Well
entries.flavour: One well, long queues, and the dry months coming.
entries.good: Water for all, even in a drought.
entries.bad: The diggers want paying, and they keep hitting scarstone.

entries.title: Pave the Market Square
entries.flavour: Mud to flagstone, fit for a city.
entries.good: Traders linger; the town looks the part.
entries.bad: A whole season's coin, sunk into the ground.

entries.title: Ring the Festival
entries.flavour: A feast day on the guild's coin, and the clapperless bell rung anyway.
entries.good: Spirits soar; both loyalty and trade rise.
entries.bad: A day's work lost, and a day's coin with it.

entries.title: Tithe to the Chapel
entries.flavour: Fund the temple and light every candle.
entries.good: The faithful are glad; the sick are tended.
entries.bad: Coin the walls could have used.

entries.title: Open the Gates to Refugees
entries.flavour: Folk fleeing the scar-lands crowd the Ford by the hundred.
entries.good: New hands for the fields and the wall.
entries.bad: More mouths to feed - and sickness travels with them.

entries.title: Hire the Sellswords
entries.flavour: Coin for blades that answer to gold, not the guild.
entries.good: Hard muscle for the hard floors.
entries.bad: They stay bought only as long as you keep paying.

entries.title: Shut the Border
entries.flavour: No stranger past the Ford without the guild's word.
entries.good: No raider walks in wearing a traveller's coat.
entries.bad: Trade withers, and the town turns inward and small.

disasters._note: Natural disasters (D34). For each: begin (Chronicle line), during (lines while it lasts), pass (line when it ends), cost (plain statement of what it should cost the town, for the desktop to implement). Dead until wired.
disasters._note_variants: Added C-cycle 11: begin_alt and pass_alt (arrays) sit beside begin and pass on EVERY disaster, and during is widened to 8 lines each. begin/pass are unchanged and still the single canonical line - a picker may roll begin_alt/pass_alt instead so a second volcano does not read word for word like the first. Additive; dead until wired.

volcano.begin: The mountain above the scar wakes - ash on the wind, and the sky goes copper.
during: Ash falls on Bellmire; the sun is a dull coin behind the smoke.
The river runs grey, and the fish float up dead.
Cinders tick off the roof-tiles all night; nobody opens a shutter.
The crier reads the day's news through a cloth over his mouth.
The ash drifts into the grain store through a gap nobody knew was there.
Sheep come down off the high pasture coughing, and do not go back up.
The chapel bell rings muffled, packed with grey.
Children write their names in the ash on the shutters. By morning it has written over them.
volcano.pass: The mountain settles. Ash greys every roof, but the air clears.
volcano.cost: A buried harvest and sickened livestock; the worst-hit district must be rebuilt.
begin_alt: Grit on the tongue before dawn - the mountain is awake, and the sky turns copper.
The mountain clears its throat. Ash comes down on Bellmire like slow snow.
Ash on the wind out of the high country. Shutter the stores.
pass_alt: The mountain goes quiet. Bellmire shovels grey off its roofs and breathes clean.
The ashfall stops. Every rooftop wears a winter nobody ordered.
The sky loses its copper. The sweeping will take a month.

fire.begin: Fire in Craft Row - a forge banked wrong, and the wind unkind.
during: The bucket line runs from the river; the Watch beats at the flames.
Smoke rolls over the square as the smiths' roofs go up.
Craft Row is a tunnel of heat; the Watch wets the next roof down and waits.
Somebody's apprentice runs back in for the tools and is dragged out again.
The wind turns, and the bucket line turns with it, cursing.
A roof-beam goes down and the whole square flinches.
They pull a smith off his own forge; he fights them the whole way out.
Sparks ride the night air toward the thatch, and every eye follows them up.
fire.pass: The fire is out. A row of workshops is char and cinder.
fire.cost: Buildings in one district burned down and rebuilt from nothing; the smiths sit idle until then.
begin_alt: Craft Row is alight - a banked forge, a bad wind, and no rain since market day.
Fire. The word crosses the square faster than the smoke does.
Flame in the workshops, and the Watch are up before the bell is.
pass_alt: The last roof falls in and stays down. The fire is finished.
The flames are beaten out at the row's end. What is left is char and cinder.
It is over. Craft Row smokes, and the smiths stand looking at it.

drought.begin: No rain since the thaw. The river drops, and the wells go shy.
during: The crops stand yellow and brittle in the field.
The queue at the well starts before dawn.
The mill-wheel stands still in a riverbed of stones.
Dust comes off the fields in sheets and settles on the market bread.
The well rope goes down further each morning and comes up lighter.
Dust walks the cart-track where the mud used to be.
The miller stops the wheel. There is no water to turn it.
Cattle are driven to the Ford and find it ankle-deep.
drought.pass: Rain, at last. The river climbs, and Bellmire drinks easy again.
drought.cost: A harvest cut to nothing and thinning livestock; morale sinks until the wells fill.
begin_alt: No rain since the thaw. The fields crack, and the river shows its bones.
The sky stays empty. The wells go shy and the Ford goes shallow.
A dry season settles on Bellmire and shows no sign of leaving.
pass_alt: Rain. The whole town stands out in it and lets it happen.
The river climbs back up its banks, and the wells answer again.
The drought breaks in one grey afternoon. Nobody complains about the mud.

famine.begin: The barns are near bare, and spring is a long way off.
during: Rations at the guild post; the thin get thinner.
A copper will not buy bread that is not there.
The guild post weighs every portion and still sends people away short.
Children are fed first, and the adults have agreed not to discuss it.
The barn is measured twice a day now, and the number never improves.
The guild post cuts the ration and does not meet anyone's eye.
Folk eat the seed grain, which is tomorrow eaten today.
A family leaves for downriver in the dark, so nobody has to say goodbye.
famine.pass: The first harvest comes in, and Bellmire eats again.
famine.cost: The town shrinks as the weak are lost; no growth until the barns refill.
begin_alt: The barns are near bare. Measure the grain - there is not much to measure.
Winter has outlasted the harvest, and Bellmire starts counting mouths.
The stores run down to the bottom boards, and spring is a long way off.
pass_alt: The first cart of grain comes in. The square goes quiet, then very loud.
The barns fill. Bellmire eats a whole meal and remembers how.
The harvest lands. The hungry season has a last day, and this is it.

sickness.begin: A fever walks the homes. The apothecary names it, then runs short of cures.
during: Doors chalked with a warning mark; the healers do not sleep.
The chapel bell tolls more than anyone likes.
The healers run out of simples before they run out of patients.
Market day is called off; the square has never looked bigger.
Doors are marked in chalk, and the chalk is running out.
The apothecary works the night through and brews water with a name on it.
The chapel keeps its lamps lit for the ones who will not see morning.
The Watch carry food to the marked doors and set it down without knocking.
sickness.pass: The fever burns itself out. Bellmire counts its dead and opens the windows.
sickness.cost: The population falls, and a quarantine freezes trade and work while it lasts.
begin_alt: A fever is in the homes. It has a name by noon and no cure by dusk.
Sickness walks Bellmire door to door, politely, and does not stop.
The apothecary shutters the shop to brew, and that tells the town everything.
pass_alt: The fever lets go. The windows open, and the chalk comes off the doors.
The last marked door is scrubbed clean. Bellmire counts its dead and goes on.
It burns out. The chapel rings for the lost, and then for the rest of us.

hurricane.begin: A great storm drives inland, and the sky turns the colour of a bruise.
during: Roofs peel away; the river bursts its low banks.
Nobody walks the wall in this.
The gate bar is doubled and the horses are brought inside the hall.
Something large goes past the window sideways and nobody goes to look.
Thatch goes over the square in sheets, like a flock that forgot how.
The Watch rope themselves together to cross the open ground.
Every shutter in Bellmire is either barred or gone.
The river comes up the lane and knocks at the low doors.
hurricane.pass: The storm blows through. Bellmire is sodden and battered, but standing.
hurricane.cost: Roofs and buildings torn across the town, fields flooded, and days of repair.
begin_alt: A great storm drives inland, and the horizon turns the colour of an old bruise.
The gulls came inland yesterday. Now we know why.
Storm off the water, with the whole valley to cross and nothing in its way.
pass_alt: The storm goes over the hills. Bellmire is sodden, battered and standing.
The wind drops. What is left on the roofs stayed because it was nailed.
The sky clears out. Count the roofs, then count the people.

tornado.begin: A finger of wind drops out of the storm and walks toward the town.
during: It takes a barn whole and sets it down in splinters.
Mind the sky - it has not lifted yet.
Carts are roped to posts and the posts are not reassuring.
It walks the far field twice and turns, and the whole town watches the turn.
It takes the fence line, the hay cart and the cart's horse, in that order.
The sound arrives before the wind does, and nobody forgets it.
Folk go flat in the ditches and hold on to the grass.
A door lands in the square. Nobody owns it.
tornado.pass: The wind lifts and is gone, leaving a straight scar of wreckage.
tornado.cost: A random line of buildings flattened, and livestock scattered or lost.
begin_alt: A finger of wind drops out of the cloud and starts walking toward Bellmire.
The storm grows a tail, and the tail touches the fields.
Something is coming across the barley in a straight line.
pass_alt: The wind lifts. It left a straight road of wreckage through the town.
Gone as fast as it came, and it took a line of Bellmire with it.
The air goes still. The damage is a stripe you could walk end to end.

earthquake.begin: The ground rolls - the scar shudders, and so does everything above it.
during: Walls crack; the clapperless bell swings and almost rings.
Aftershocks, and nobody trusts a roof.
The well comes up muddy and the masons will not say why yet.
Every door in Bellmire sticks, and one wall leans that did not lean before.
The bell with no clapper rings anyway, and nobody finds that funny tonight.
Masonry comes off the gatehouse in the aftershock.
Folk sleep in the square rather than under their own beams.
A crack opens along the chapel floor and runs out under the door.
earthquake.pass: The shaking stops. Bellmire checks its walls, and its dead.
earthquake.cost: Walls and buildings cracked or down town-wide; the scar may gape a little deeper.
begin_alt: The ground rolls. The scar shudders, and everything above it shudders with it.
Bellmire moves - all of it, at once, and the wrong way.
A sound out of the deep, and then the whole town is standing on water.
pass_alt: The shaking stops. Bellmire walks its own walls looking for daylight.
It settles. The masons are out before the dust is down.
The ground holds still. The town checks its walls, and its dead.

meteor.begin: A star falls - too slow, too bright - and comes down past the fields.
during: The impact lights the night; the ground is scorched for a mile.
Something glitters in the new crater, and it hums like the scar.
Carters give the crater a wide berth; the horses refuse it outright.
The scar hums all night, as if something answered.
The orchard burns in rows, tree after tree, very neatly.
The crater glows all night and hums if you stand too close.
The first fool down the crater wall comes back up with a fistful of glass.
The guild post has a man on the crater by morning, counting.
meteor.pass: The fires burn out. A crater smokes where the orchard used to stand.
meteor.cost: An outlying district or the orchard is destroyed - but the crater yields scarglass worth a fortune.
begin_alt: A star falls - too slow, too bright - and the fields take it.
Something comes down past the orchard, and the night turns white.
The sky drops a burning thing on Bellmire's edge.
pass_alt: The fires die back. A crater smokes where the orchard stood.
It burns out by dawn. What is left is a hole full of glass.
The last tree stops burning. The crater is already worth a fortune.

scarstorm.begin: The scar flares, and wild magic rolls up out of the dungeon mouth and over the town.
during: Every spell cast in Bellmire goes wrong; the lamps burn strange colours.
The livestock speak for a heartbeat, and the well runs uphill.
The apothecary corks everything and sits on the box.
A delver's lamp burns green, and the dark leans in to look.
A door opens onto a different room than it did this morning.
Every candle in the chapel burns blue and will not be put out.
A cooper's barrel fills itself with river water, and nobody touches it.
The casters sit it out, hands in their laps, useless and insulted.
scarstorm.pass: The scar quiets. The magic settles, mostly, and the town tallies what changed.
scarstorm.cost: Spellcasters are useless while it lasts; random buildings warp, and a few folk are scar-touched for good or ill.
begin_alt: The scar flares. Wild magic rolls out of the dungeon mouth and over the roofs.
The scar breathes out, and what it breathes is not air.
Magic comes up out of the scar in a wave, looking for somewhere to land.
pass_alt: The scar quiets. The magic settles - mostly - and the tally begins.
It passes. Bellmire checks what changed, and what changed back.
The wave rolls off. Two or three folk are scar-touched now, for good or ill.

flood.begin: The thaw comes all at once. The river climbs the banks, and keeps climbing.
during: The low district is ankle-deep, then knee-deep.
The Ford is gone under brown water; no crossing today.
The grain store is moved up a floor by every pair of hands in town.
Boats in the lane where carts should be, and someone fishing out of a window.
The Ford is gone - only the posts show where it was.
Stores go up to the Keep a sack at a time, through knee-deep water.
A hen coop sails past the chapel with the hens still aboard.
The Watch mark the water on the gatepost each hour. The marks keep climbing.
flood.pass: The water drops back, leaving mud in every doorway - but the town held.
flood.cost: Riverside buildings and stores ruined; the Ford and its trade shut until the river falls.
begin_alt: The thaw comes all at once. The river climbs the bank and does not stop.
The river is over the low fields by noon and over the lane by dark.
Water in the doorways - the Ford has given up being a ford.
pass_alt: The water drops back. Mud in every doorway, and the town held.
The river goes home. It left most of its bed in Bellmire's front rooms.
The flood falls away. The Ford shows its posts again, and the trade with them.

blight.begin: A black rot is in the grain - it came up in one field and did not stop there.
during: Whole rows are cut and burned before the rot can walk to the next field.
The miller turns away sack after sack, and says nothing, which is worse.
The rot shows black at the stalk and climbs from there.
Field hands burn their gloves at the end of the day, just in case.
Bread goes up a copper, then another, and the baker stops apologising.
The guild post buys grain from downriver at a price it will not read aloud.
A farmer stands at his field edge all afternoon doing nothing at all.
They plough the worst acre under and sow nothing in it.
blight.pass: The blight burns out at the field edge. What is left of the harvest comes in early.
blight.cost: Most of the standing harvest is lost; food prices climb and the stores do not refill this season.
begin_alt: Black rot in the grain. It started in one field and did not stay there.
The harvest has something in it, and the something is spreading.
A blight walks the fields row by row, taking its time.
pass_alt: The blight stops at the field edge. What is left comes in early and thin.
The rot burns out. Bellmire salvages whatever the fire did not reach.
It ends. The barns take a half-harvest and are told to make it do.

coldsnap.begin: The cold comes early and hard - the Ford freezes over in a night.
during: Firewood costs what wine cost last week, and the queue for it is longer.
The Watch walk in pairs now, because one man alone stops moving.
The Ford is a road now, and nobody trusts it enough to use it.
The forge is the warmest room in Bellmire, and the smith charges for the privilege.
Water freezes in the bucket between the well and the door.
Caravans turn back at the hill, and the market has empty boards.
They bring the lambs indoors and share the floor with them.
The chapel takes in whoever has no fire, and the chapel is full.
coldsnap.pass: The thaw comes. The Ford runs again, and Bellmire counts who it kept.
coldsnap.cost: Livestock lost and work stopped: building, trade and the fields all halt until the thaw.
begin_alt: The cold comes early and hard, and the Ford freezes over in a night.
Winter arrives a month ahead of schedule and makes itself at home.
Ice on the inside of the shutters by morning. This will be a bad one.
pass_alt: The thaw comes. The Ford runs, and Bellmire counts who it kept.
The ice gives up. Water moves again, and so does the town.
The cold breaks. The first cart over the Ford gets a cheer it did not expect.

events._note: Random world events (D33): bandit and monster camps that stand until cleared, and a wandering boss scaled to the town's level. Dead until wired.
events._note_variants: Added C-cycle 11: 3 more bandit camps (4 -> 7), 3 more monster camps (3 -> 6) in the same key shape, and appears_alt / while_alt / cleared_alt on wandering_boss - there is only one wandering boss, so its three lines would otherwise repeat verbatim every time it walks. Additive; dead until wired.

bandit_camps.name: The Gallows Oak
bandit_camps.appears: Red Harl's lot have taken the west road. No caravan reaches the Ford unbled.
bandit_camps.while: Trade caravans are robbed; the market runs short and prices climb.
bandit_camps.cleared: Red Harl hangs from his own Gallows Oak. The west road is open again.

bandit_camps.name: The Mire Nest
bandit_camps.appears: Sedge the Toll holds the fen path and taxes everyone who is not her.
bandit_camps.while: Every trader by the fen pays Sedge first; the town's cut shrinks.
bandit_camps.cleared: Sedge the Toll pays her own toll at last. The fen path clears.

bandit_camps.name: The Burnt Mill
bandit_camps.appears: Cob Ashfoot's raiders have holed up in the burnt mill, firing a field a night to keep the town afraid.
bandit_camps.while: A field burns most nights; harvest and morale both drop.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Burnt Mill burns one last time. Cob Ashfoot runs, and keeps running.

bandit_camps.name: Scarside Camp
bandit_camps.appears: The Weasel's crew squat at the scar's edge, robbing the delvers who climb out.
bandit_camps.while: Returning delvers are waylaid; their gold and loot never reach Bellmire.
bandit_camps.cleared: Scarside Camp is cleared. Delvers come up to friends now, not knives.

bandit_camps.name: The Drover's Rest
bandit_camps.appears: Juno Blackhand has taken the drovers' inn on the north road and left the sign hanging.
bandit_camps.while: Livestock driven to market never arrive; the pens stand empty on market day.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Drover's Rest changes hands again. Juno Blackhand does not leave with it.

bandit_camps.name: The Quarry Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Old Peck's lot have moved into the worked-out quarry and are selling Bellmire its own stone back.
bandit_camps.while: Cut stone and lime go missing; building in town stalls for want of either.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Quarry Camp is emptied out. The stone comes down the road at an honest price.

bandit_camps.name: The Lampless Road
bandit_camps.appears: Wick Harrow's crew put out the road lamps one by one, and work the dark they made.
bandit_camps.while: Nobody travels after dusk; the night trade stops and the Ford shuts early.
bandit_camps.cleared: The lamps burn the whole length of the road again. Wick Harrow walks it in chains.

monster_camps.name: The Bone Field
monster_camps.appears: Something below spat up its dead, and they are gathering in the north field.
monster_camps.while: The dead multiply nightly and gnaw at the outlying farms.
monster_camps.cleared: The Bone Field is put down. The north field is only a field again.

monster_camps.name: The Slime Warren
monster_camps.appears: A slime nest has taken the old quarry, and it doubles every night it is left alone.
monster_camps.while: The quarry is lost, and the nest creeps toward the homes.
monster_camps.cleared: The Slime Warren is burned out. The quarry stops twitching.

monster_camps.name: The Belltower Roost
monster_camps.appears: A roost of cave bats has taken the bell-tower; they foul the wells and spook every horse in town.
monster_camps.while: The wells need watching, and the beasts are restless while they hang there.
monster_camps.cleared: The Roost is cleared. The bell-tower is quiet. Almost.

monster_camps.name: The Sedge Mound
monster_camps.appears: The fen has gone loud - bog frogs the size of dogs have mounded up in the sedge.
monster_camps.while: The fen path is lost, and the fishers work the river or not at all.
monster_camps.cleared: The Sedge Mound is cleared. The fen is merely unpleasant again.

monster_camps.name: The Silk Barn
monster_camps.appears: A barn on the south road has gone white - cave spiders came up out of the scar and took it.
monster_camps.while: The south road is spun shut; nothing moves past the barn after dusk.
monster_camps.cleared: The Silk Barn burns. The south road is clear, and nothing is watching it.

monster_camps.name: The Gnaw Pits
monster_camps.appears: Scar rats have got into the old root pits, and they are not the size rats are meant to be.
monster_camps.while: Stores are gnawed through nightly; what the town keeps, it keeps losing.
monster_camps.cleared: The Gnaw Pits are flooded out. The stores hold their weight overnight again.

wandering_boss.name: The Scarred Lord
wandering_boss.appears: A lord has climbed out of the scar and walks the open country - and it has grown to match the town it hunts.
wandering_boss.while: It razes an outlying farm each day it roams, and draws the dark along behind it.
wandering_boss.cleared: The wandering lord falls in the open field. Bellmire drags the body home as proof.
wandering_boss.note: Scales to the town's level: a lesser lord early, a greater lord once Bellmire is a city. Reuse the eight canon lords; never a new one.
appears_alt: Something that should be under the scar is walking the open country, and it has grown to fit the town it is coming for.
A lord has climbed out of the dark and taken to the fields. It gets larger the nearer it comes.
The scar let one out. It is wearing the shape of the town's own strength.
while_alt: A holding goes dark each night it roams, and the dark follows it home.
It burns an outlying farm a day and drags the deep country along behind it.
Nothing stays settled where it walks; the far farms empty ahead of it.
cleared_alt: The wandering lord goes down in the open field, in daylight, in front of everyone.
It falls at last on honest ground. Bellmire hauls the carcass back as proof.
The lord is put down outside the walls. The farms come back one cart at a time.

growth_tiers._note: Town growth stages (D31/D32) - the town levels far too fast, so this is a long, earned climb. For each: the stage name, the crier's line on reaching it, and what a viewer should SEE appear. Complements town_levels_for_the_desktop (coarser, 7 levels). Dead until wired.

tiers.name: Crossing
tiers.crier: A handful of huts at a river crossing. Somebody calls it Bellmire.
tiers.see: Three or four huts, a cart, a cookfire.

tiers.name: Hamlet
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a hamlet now - a well dug, and a reason to stay.
tiers.see: A well, a few more homes, a fenced garden or two.

tiers.name: The Guild Post
tiers.crier: The guild plants a post at Bellmire. The post has a door, and the door is kept.
tiers.see: The guild post building, and the town's first lamp.

tiers.name: Village
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a village. The scar has a name, and so do we.
tiers.see: Homes clustered along a cart-track, chickens, a shared pen.

tiers.name: Market Day
tiers.crier: Market day comes to Bellmire. Measure the grain.
tiers.see: A market square with a few stalls, and the first outside traders.

tiers.name: The Chapel
tiers.crier: A chapel and a bell-tower rise. The bell has no clapper, and rings anyway.
tiers.see: The temple and its tower, and a small graveyard behind it.

tiers.name: Craft Row
tiers.crier: The smiths and masons raise Craft Row. Count the flasks.
tiers.see: Workshops trailing smoke, a forge-glow, the mill wheel turning.

tiers.name: The Garrison
tiers.crier: Bellmire raises a garrison. The guard has a yard now - and a Commander.
tiers.see: Barracks and a training yard, guards on patrol, E3PO up on the wall.

tiers.name: Market Town
tiers.crier: Bellmire stands as a proper market town. The caravans know the road.
tiers.see: A paved square, more districts, a busy Ford with its Ferryman.

tiers.name: The First Wall
tiers.crier: Stone goes up where the fields used to stop. Keep the door.
tiers.see: A low wall around the town's heart, and a gatehouse over the road.

tiers.name: Walled Town
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a walled town now. Let them come.
tiers.see: A full curtain wall, corner towers, a district banner on each quarter.

tiers.name: City in all but Charter
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a city in all but the charter - and the scar is deeper than it has ever been.
tiers.see: Dense districts, a second ring of homes outside the wall, traffic at every gate.
